searchText: Have you tested withdrawals with 0 amount? https://github.com/ethereum/tests/blob/develop/BlockchainTests/InvalidBlocks/bc4895-withdrawals/amountIs0.json Also here: https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/blob/6363b17fb61efcb2fd4df08092d2d3e96588449d/fillers/withdrawals/withdrawals.py#L593 This is confusing. The spec says amount cannot be 0. Are such withdrawals invalid? I think the "nonzero" description is because of the assumption that the beacon chain can never deliver a zero value, but it doesn't specifically say that a zero value should be rejected EELS currently accepts zero value withdrawals as valid. Yes, t8n also calculate the poststate of withdrawal 0 https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-4895#system-level-operation-withdrawal > a nonzero amount of ether given in Gwei (1e9 wei) as a uint64 value. Even if we assume the amount can be 0 it is under-specified how this is handled. E.g. does it touch the target account?
